subject: mass-communication
title: Television Programme Production
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The first stage of programme production is —
Which function is performed during the pre-production stage of a television programme?
______ and ______ are part of the pre-production stage.
The most basic equipment in any production is the —
What converts sound waves into electrical signals?
Who is in charge of all activities on the studio floor?
Who is the head of the television production and manages the budget?
Cutting recorded visuals to the appropriate length is part of —
Which is an advantage of live programmes?
The art director is in charge of —
options: creative design aspects such as sets and graphics

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Match: (i) Art Director (ii) Cameraperson with (a) Handles visuals (b) Handles creative design aspects.
Match: (i) Script writers (ii) Anchor with (a) Writes for programmes (b) Presents programmes.

State true or false: (i) Lighting any object or individual establishes the general mood of the event in television production. (ii) The Production Assistant facilitates all that is required for the smooth execution of the television production.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are part of the pre-production stage.
Fill in the blanks: A television camera converts the ______ image into ______ signals.
Arrange in order: post-production, pre-production, production.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: List any two types of equipment and their functions used in studio recording.
questions.answer: Microphone converts sound into electrical signals; camera converts the optical image into a video signal (also lights illuminate, sound recorder records and mixes sound).

questions.q: Briefly describe the work profile of any two of: Art Director, Costume Designer, Property Manager.
questions.answer: Art Director is in charge of creative design (sets, location, graphics); Costume Designer designs and sometimes constructs costumes.

questions.q: What is post-production?
questions.answer: The stage of final shaping: cutting, sequencing, effects, captions, commentary, music and final assembly.

questions.q: What is the role of a floor manager?
questions.answer: He is in charge of all activities on the studio floor, conveys the director's instructions and supervises floor personnel.

questions.q: Differentiate between studio and outdoor recording.
questions.answer: Studio recording is within the four walls of a studio; outdoor recording is shooting outside it.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the stages of television programme production.
questions.answer: Pre-production: idea, research, script, arranging equipment and sets. Production: shooting with the crew and talent on the floor or location. Post-production: editing, captions, commentary, music and final assembly.

questions.q: Describe the roles of the producer, director and script writer.
questions.answer: The producer heads the production, budget and coordination; the director directs actors and technical operations and turns the script into audio-visuals; the script writer writes dialogues, costumes, mood and locations.

questions.q: Compare live and recorded programmes.
questions.answer: Live programmes generate excitement and can be made speedily but depend on the crew's performance; recorded programmes allow retakes and editing and market better but lack excitement.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the production process of a television programme with the equipment required.
questions.answer: Three stages: pre-production (idea, script), production (shooting with camera, lights, microphone and sound recorder) and post-production (editing on the editing machine); the team includes producer, director, anchor and crew.

questions.q: Describe the work profile of the key professionals involved in programme production.
questions.answer: Producer, director, production assistant, script writer, actors, anchor, cameraperson, sound recordist, art director, property manager, floor manager and costume designer each play a crucial role in the team effort.
